text: If I ask a dude, hey, are you a feminist and they want to start Well, like define feminist cuz like the radical extremism wrap it up. I've heard enough wrap it up. You're done wrap it up Come on Well, here's the thing Can you actually define feminism because last time I checked even researchers don't treat feminism as one single idea a very common way To describe it is through four different ways and those waves are quite different from each other So when someone says I'm a feminist What exactly do you mean and this is where the real problem starts because a lot of women and some men Today who call themselves feminists don't actually know what feminism is. They can't clearly define it They don't know where it comes from. They don't know who shaped it They just have a very vague idea and repeat what they've heard and then the moment someone asks for a definition It is suddenly wrap it up But defining it actually matters because first wave feminism is not the same as fourth wave feminism Not even close first wave basic legal rights second wave equality in society and workplace and I'll say this openly I agree with a lot of what those movements stood for but when we get into third and fourth wave ideas Which are much more complex things become much more controversial. That's where I personally have quite a few questions So again, when you say feminism, which version are you talking about because without that you are not having a discussion You're just throwing around a label and this is exactly why I'm starting this series Mansplaining feminism now since most of my viewers are men some of you might ask why should men even care about this? Well, let me tell you why first it's part of our history And if you live in a society, it is good to understand how it was shaped Second we all have women in our lives that we deeply care about mothers sisters partners classmates co-workers and so on So understanding the ideas that affect and influence them is quite important and third if you ever get into a discussion about feminism It's probably better to actually know what you're talking about instead of reacting emotionally or repeating slogans Will it always help? No, but still knowledge is power and in this series We're going to do exactly that break it down properly Where feminism comes from what each wave actually stood for who shaped the movement and where things started getting controversial? Because before you support something or criticize it you should at least understand it
